title: Which three-place contacts are rigid in direction: stripes and straight walls, not algebra
claim: The 30 three-place tiling contacts split into four kinds by their doubly allowed and coin-pinned patterns. Polymorphisms do not separate rigid from selective contacts: all are trivial, and renaming the places of one relation can change its kind. Contacts with stripes contradict at most along the diagonal class, or never; contacts whose walls cannot turn at an end of the diagonal edge contradict along all odd classes or none, with an exact count; the twelve whose walls can turn are selective on 3 x 3, and for the four with no free place an odd class contradicts exactly when every valid wall cycle collides with its own copy on that cylinder.
failure_conditions: A configuration of a stripe or straight-wall placement whose contradiction set is selective, or a straight-wall count that differs from the formula.
A configuration of placement 54, 109, 147 or 151 whose certified pattern differs from the rotating-wall rule.
foundation_claim_scope: Twisted fair worlds on triangular tori with cylinder covers; exact statements and finite computations. Lattices are declared; no space or physics is claimed.
